The Court made the following:
Judgment:

-
Challenge in this M.A.C.M.A. is to the award, dated 22.01.2016, in M.V.O.P.No.197 of 2012, on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - cum - I Additional District Judge, Kurnool Claims Officer, Chennai vs B C Maddilety, Kurnool Dist 2 Others on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152915214/
1 (Tribunal for short), whereunder the Tribunal dealing with claim for compensation made by the claimant for a sum of Rs.3,50,000/-, towards compensation, with regard to the death of the deceased by name Bogi Yellaswamy, who died in a motor vehicle accident, which was occurred on 16.12.2009 at 05.30 p.m., near Muniswamy Metta, on N.H.18 road, in between Nannur Village to Kurnool Town, Orvakal Mandal, awarded a sum of Rs.3,50,000/-.
2. The parties to this M.A.C.M.A. will hereinafter be referred to as described before the learned Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. The case of the claimant before the Tribunal, in brief, according to the averments set out in the Motor Vehicle accident claim, is that:
(i) The petitioners Nos.1 and 2 are the parents of the deceased Bogi Yellaswamy, who died in the alleged accident.
Respondent No.1 is the owner of the Qualis car bearing No. AP 04 H 4788 (offending vehicle for short).
Respondent No.2 is the insurer, with which the offending vehicle is insured.
The policy is valid from 02.12.2009 to 01.12.2010.
(ii) The deceased was working as mason.
On 16.12.2009, the deceased along with his friend M.Mohammed Khasim @ Munna, started to Kurnool from Nannur village on a motor cycle bearing No. AP 21 P 9880.
The deceased was pillion rider and Munna was rider of the said motorcycle.

At about 05.30 p.m., when they reached near Muniswamy Metta on N.H.18 road, on left side of the road, one Qualis car bearing No. AP 04 H 4788, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, came in a wrong route and hit the said motor cycle.
As a result, both fell down from the motorcycle, received grievous injuries and died on the spot.
In the said accident, motorcycle also burnt and completely damaged.
(iii) The deceased was aged 19 years.
He was hale and health prior to the accident.
He was working as mason and used to earn Rs.200/- per day.
Due to the sudden demise of the deceased, petitioner Nos.1 and 2 lost love and affection and financial distress condition as the deceased was sole bread winner of the his family.
Hence, the claim for Rs.3,50,000/-.

(iv) The accident was occurred purely because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Qualis car and on the strength of the complaint given by one K.Naga Maddaiah, V.R.O., Nannur Village, a case was registered.
Both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
4. (i) Respondent No.1 remained exparte.
Respondent No.2 got filed counter, contending in substance that the petitioners have to prove the age, occupation and income of the deceased.

(ii) Additional counter was filed by the respondent No.2, stating that the criminal case records shows that the deceased drove the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner at high speed and went in wrong route to the right side of the road and dashed the Qualis vehicle, which was coming in Claims Officer, Chennai vs B C Maddilety, Kurnool Dist 2 Others on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152915214/
2 the opposite direction and killed himself and the rider.

sentences.text: Police abated case as the driver of the motorcycle who was accused in the case was also died.
The petitioners filed the present claim against the respondent Nos.1 and 2 with false allegations.
The respondent No.1 was not responsible for causing the accident as well the death of the deceased.
Hence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation and the claim is liable to be dismissed.

5. Basing on the above pleadings, the Tribunal settled the following issue for trial:
(1) Whether the accident took place as stated in the petition?
(2) Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, to what amount and which of respondents?

(3) To what relief?
6.
During the course of trial, before the Tribunal, on behalf of the petitioners, PWs.1 and 2 were examined.
Exs. A1
to A4 were marked.
On behalf of the contesting respondents, RWs.1 and 2 were examined.
Ex.B1 Insurance Policy was marked.

7. The Tribunal on hearing both sides and on considering the oral as well as documentary evidence, answered the issues in favour of the claimants and against the respondents, awarded a sum of Rs.3,50,000/-, towards compensation.

8. Felt aggrieved of the aforesaid award, the unsuccessful respondent No.2, filed the present M.A.C.M.A.
9.

Now, in deciding the present M.A.C.M.A., the point determination is as follows:
"Whether the award, dated 22.01.2016, in M.V.O.P.No.197 of 2012, on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - cum - I Additional District Judge,
Kurnool, is sustainable under law and facts and whether there are any grounds to interfere with the same?"
POINT:
10.

sentences.text: The contention of Sri Kota Subba Rao, learned counsel for the appellant originally is that in a claim under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act (the M.V.Act for short), the Tribunal awarded excessive compensation, which needs interference.
His contention is that the deceased who was a pillion rider involved in the accident and the rider of the motorbike has no driving license and the accident occurred was on his own negligence.
When this Court sought for certain clarification the learned counsel for the appellant brought to the notice of the Court certain facts which are born out from the record.

The observations made by the Court on 14.03.2024 as follows:
Claims Officer, Chennai vs B C Maddilety, Kurnool Dist 2 Others on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152915214/
3

sentences.text: "Heard further arguments of learned counsel for the appellant.

Learned counsel for the appellant brought to the notice of the Court that as per II Schedule pertaining to 163(A) of the M.V. Act, as the deceased was aged about 19 years as on the date of death proper multiplier should be "16" instead of "19" and the Tribunal arrived at the calculations of Rs.7,60,000/-(19X40,000) which is erroneous.
He would submit that as the deceased was bachelor, the 50% of the amount has to be deducted and the proper multiplier "16" has to be applied.
If that is done the compensation would accounts to Rs.6,40,000/-(16X40,000) and half of the amount is Rs.3,20,000/-.

Apart from that the claimants are entitled to conventional amounts of Rs.7,000/-
according to structured formula basis.
So he would submit that the compensation should be reduced appropriately to that of Rs.3,50,000/-."

No arguments are advanced on behalf of the respondent Nos.1 and 2.
11.
As seen from the claim before the Tribunal, it was laid under Section 163-A of the M.V.Act.
Though there was no need to prove the fault or negligence against the driver of the offending vehicle, but the pleadings were made as if the driver of the offending vehicle was negligent.
Even PW.1 testified the same in her examination.
Further the claimants examined PW.2 in support of that.

It is to be noted that as there is no need to prove rash and negligent act in a claim under Section 163-A of the M.V.Act, it is sufficient on the part claimants to prove that the death of the deceased was caused on account of the usage of offending vehicle.
Insofar as that aspect is concerned, it was categorically established by the claimants.
12. Now, turning to the quantum of compensation, the claimants pleaded that the deceased was aged 19 years and was earning Rs.200/-, per day.

The Tribunal considered the fact that the claim was laid under Section 163-A of the M.V.Act and considering the age of the deceased, arrived at the compensation of Rs.7,60,000/- ,deducted 1/2 of the amount towards personal and living expenses and awarded Rs.4,500/-, per month towards notional income and arrived Rs.3,84,500/- and restricted the claim to a tune of Rs.3,50,000/-.

13. As paragraph 12 of the award did not show any reasons, this Court sought for clarification and on account of the above of the learned counsel for the appellant made clarification as extracted above.

The paragraph No.12 of the award of the Tribunal runs as follows:
"12.There is no dispute with regard to the relationship of the deceased with the petitioners.
The pleading and evidence of petitioners is that deceased was aged about 19 years and was earning Rs.200/- per day.
But the petition filed under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act, petitioners are entitled for compensation as contemplated in II schedule of the Motor Vehicles Act.
According to the II Schedule of the Motor vehicles act, considering the age of the deceased as 19 years he is entitled for Rs.7,60,000/-.
Since the deceased is the bachelor, hence half of the income of the deceased can be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Then, it works out to Rs.7,60,000/2 = Rs.3,80,000/-.

Apart from the petitioners are entitled Rs.2,000/-
Claims Officer, Chennai vs B C Maddilety, Kurnool Dist 2 Others on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152915214/
4 towards funeral expenses and Rs.2,500/- towards loss of estate.
In total the petitioners are entitled to Rs.3,84,500/-.
But the petitioners are restricted their claim to Rs.3,50,000/-.
Hence, Rs.3,50,000/- is awarded towards the compensation."
14. Now, according to the claimants, the deceased was earning Rs.200/-, per day.
The maximum income which the claimants can claim in view of the structured formula under Section 163-A of the M.V.Act is only Rs.40,000/-.
The Tribunal wrongly applied multiplier of 19 i.e., the age of the deceased with Rs.40,000/- and arrived at Rs.7,60,000/-.
It is not that the Tribunal has to consider only the maximum amount.
Infact, the period of accident was in the year 2009.
During the said period, even a manual labour could easily get Rs.100/- per day.
Considering the same, appropriate income which the Tribunal has to consider is as that of Rs.36,000/- per year.
The proper multiplier only 16.
According to the structured formula 1/3rd of the amount has to be deducted from the total income, as such, it would amounts to Rs.24,000/- per annum.

If it is multiplied with multiplier 16,
as per the structured formula, it would amount to Rs.3,84,000/-.
Further apart from that, claimant are entitled under the conventional heads of Rs.2,500/- and Rs.2,000/-, in view of the structured formula.
So, compensation of Rs.3,50,000/- awarded is not at all excessive.
There is no cross objection or appeal filed by the appellant and they did not contest the appeal.

Hence, there is no need to interfere with the quantum of the compensation of Rs.3,50,000/-.
15.
In the result, the M.A.C.M.A. is dismissed, but, under the circumstances, without costs.

The appellant shall deposit the rest of the compensation, if any, within a period of one month from the date of this judgment and on such deposit, the claimants are at liberty to withdraw entire compensation.
Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
JUSTICE A.V. RAVINDRA BABU Dt.06.05.2024.
